description: Baseline benchmark across all Go benchmarks with median per benchmark and geomean primary metric

asi.hypothesis: Establish stable baseline for all existing benchmarks before applying optimizations.
asi.baseline_observations: CLI parse/help benchmarks dominate geomean; NewString combines UUID generation and Base58 encode. EncodeBase58 allocates twice due external encoder plus string concatenation/padding; UUID7/FromTime allocate via crypto/rand.Int and math/big.

description: Replace math/big rand.Int UUID randomness with rand.Read and integer sub-ms precision

asi.hypothesis: Avoid crypto/rand.Int's math/big allocation path and float math while preserving UUIDv7 variant/version/output semantics.
asi.learned: Large general win: FromTime/UUID7 now zero-allocation; NewString dropped from 5 to 2 allocs because generation no longer allocates. rand.Read 8 bytes then masks variant bits is more direct and uniform for rand_b than previous big.Int path.

description: Direct fixed-width Base58 encoder reduced allocs but failed encode/decode/order tests; check output cap prevents pi crash on noisy failures

asi.hypothesis: Replacing base58.Encode with a one-allocation fixed-width encoder would reduce EncodeBase58/NewString allocations.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks fail massively: encoded strings do not match vectors, DecodeBase58 round trips fail, and lexicographic ordering breaks. The noisy TestEncodeDecode loop produced gigabytes of stdout, which is the concrete trigger for pi's Invalid string length crash.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the output-capped .auto/checks.sh; if revisiting direct Base58, implement canonical big-integer base conversion exactly or optimize around existing base58.Encode padding instead.
asi.pi_crash_cause: pi execCommand concatenates child stdout into a JS string; uncapped go test output exceeded V8 max string length at dist/core/exec.js stdout += data.toString().

description: Collapse CLI help output to a single constant WriteString and avoid fmt for generated ID newline

asi.hypothesis: printUsage currently performs many fmt.Println calls; replacing them with one constant WriteString preserves exact help text while avoiding repeated fmt dispatch and writes. Generated ID output may also avoid fmt overhead with WriteString.
asi.learned: The single constant usage write produced a very large general win for CLI help (about 8us to 0.39us). Generate path regressed in this sample likely due two direct writes/noise; primary geomean improved substantially because help was a dominant benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider testing whether generateUUID should use fmt.Println or a single write buffer rather than two WriteString calls; also optimize parseUUID output formatting/DecodeBase58 next.

description: Collapse parse output formatting into one Fprintf with shared time format constant

asi.hypothesis: parseUUID spends much of its time in many fmt.Print* calls and repeated parsing of the timestamp layout literal; one Fprintf with a shared layout constant should preserve exact CLI output while reducing dispatch and write overhead.
asi.learned: Large general win for CLI parse: BenchmarkParseUUID and BenchmarkMainParse dropped from ~5us to ~1.3us with unchanged allocation counts, confirming output call overhead dominated parse after DecodeBase58/time formatting.
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising areas: optimize DecodeBase58 allocation/path generally, or revisit generateUUID output to avoid the current two WriteString calls causing slower generate benchmarks.

description: Direct zero-allocation Base58 decode passed correctness but slowed primary geomean

asi.hypothesis: Avoid DecodeBase58's separator-removal string allocation and base58.Decode output allocation by decoding the 22 Base58 digits directly into a UUID with a lookup table, preserving valid input behavior and using the dependency only for invalid-character errors.
asi.rollback_reason: Although correctness checks passed and allocations dropped to zero for DecodeBase58, the per-digit base256 loop was much slower (DecodeBase58 ~137ns to ~249ns, EncodeDecode ~448ns to ~536ns), increasing primary geomean versus the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not use the naive direct decode algorithm. If revisiting decode, consider a faster chunked/base conversion or focus on reducing parse/output allocations elsewhere.

description: Restore fmt.Printf for generated ID output after two WriteString calls proved slower

asi.hypothesis: The prior CLI help optimization also changed generateUUID to two os.Stdout.WriteString calls; despite fewer allocations, two interface method calls/writes may be slower than the original single fmt.Printf. Restoring fmt.Printf should improve generate benchmarks without changing output.
asi.learned: Restoring fmt.Printf improved GenerateUUID/MainGenerate substantially versus the current best sample (about 1.25us to 0.93-0.98us) and improved primary geomean to ~404.7 despite one extra allocation in the CLI generate path.
asi.next_action_hint: Try a single WriteString(base58String+"\n") or preallocated []byte write as alternatives to see if single syscall/write with less fmt overhead can beat fmt.Printf while preserving output.

description: Use one WriteString call with appended newline for generated ID output

asi.hypothesis: A single os.Stdout.WriteString(base58String+"\n") should preserve exact generate output while avoiding fmt.Printf overhead and avoiding the two separate writes that previously regressed generate performance.
asi.learned: Single WriteString with concatenated newline improved GenerateUUID/MainGenerate versus restored fmt.Printf and reduced allocations back to two; primary geomean improved to ~396.5 despite small noise in encode metrics.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider a zero-extra-allocation single os.Stdout.Write over a stack [24]byte built from the encoded string plus newline, or focus on EncodeBase58 allocation count.

description: Implement correct direct fixed-width Base58 encoder with one string allocation

asi.hypothesis: A correct direct Base58 encoder can preserve the exact 22-character padded hqid7 format while avoiding base58.Encode's intermediate result allocation and the padding/separator concatenation allocations.
asi.learned: The corrected little-endian base58 conversion passed the full high-coverage encode/order tests and reduced EncodeBase58/NewString/GenerateUUID allocations to one. This contrasts with the earlier failed fixed-width encoder; the key fix was building little-endian base58 digits and reversing them into a padded raw buffer.
asi.next_action_hint: Next explore small encode micro-optimizations (combine raw/out buffers, avoid copy loops) or parse output allocation reductions; avoid the previously discarded naive direct decoder.

description: Fill final Base58 output buffer directly instead of using raw buffer and copy

asi.hypothesis: Avoid the intermediate raw [22]byte and two copy calls in EncodeBase58 by initializing the final [23]byte output with padding and writing reversed base58 digits around the separator directly.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean was slightly worse than the current best (381.09 vs 380.69). EncodeBase58 and NewString were marginally slower, likely because the extra branch/index mapping in the digit placement loop outweighed removing raw buffer copies.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler raw+copy encoder. Future encode attempts should target the base conversion loop rather than final buffer assembly, or improve parse/generate paths.

description: Format parse output into a stack byte buffer with append helpers

asi.hypothesis: Replacing parseUUID's fmt.Fprintf and time.Format string creation with AppendFormat/strconv.Append* into a stack byte buffer should preserve exact CLI output while avoiding formatting allocations and reflection overhead.
asi.learned: Large general parse win: ParseUUID/MainParse dropped from ~1.3us and 10 allocations to ~0.88us and 1 allocation. The remaining allocation is likely DecodeBase58's separator removal/base58 decode path or os.File.Write escape of the buffer.
asi.next_action_hint: Next investigate whether DecodeBase58 can remove only the separator allocation while retaining dependency speed, or reduce the final parse buffer/write allocation.

description: Specialize fixed-width binary and hex append helpers for parse output

asi.hypothesis: The generic appendFixedBase helper divides by a dynamic base for binary and hex parse output. Specialized bit-shift based appendBitsFixed and appendHexFixed should preserve exact formatting while reducing parse formatting overhead.
asi.learned: Primary geomean improved slightly to ~351.2 and ParseUUID improved to ~860ns. MainParse regressed in this sample, but the overall primary metric improved and allocations stayed at one. Gains are small and likely near noise; future confirmation may be useful.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue with broader optimizations: investigate faster safe DecodeBase58 paths or reduce generate/output overhead. Avoid relying heavily on this small parse-helper gain without more runs if subsequent noise contradicts it.

description: Implement fast fixed-width Base58 decoder using uint32 limbs

asi.hypothesis: A fixed-width hqid7 decoder can mirror mr-tron/base58's uint32-limb algorithm without allocating the separator-stripped string, rune slice, output slice, or intermediate buffers. Because hqid7 input is always exactly 22 Base58 digits plus separator, the low 128 bits map directly to the final four limbs while preserving valid decode behavior and matching dependency-style invalid digit errors.
asi.learned: This is a large general win: DecodeBase58 dropped to ~87ns and zero allocations, EncodeDecode to ~362ns and one allocation, and parse paths became zero-allocation. Unlike the earlier naive byte-array decoder, uint32 limbs keep the conversion loop small and fast.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider micro-optimizing the decoder further by unrolling six limb updates or removing fmt imports with custom errors only if invalid-error text remains acceptable; also revisit EncodeBase58 base conversion loop.
